nodes.summary: The Snell envelope dominates every conditional stopped reward (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, (1.1.9)). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space, `n ≤ N` and every stopping time `τ` with `n ≤ τ ≤ N`, `E[G τ | 𝒢 n] ≤ S n` almost everywhere.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope dominates every conditional stopped reward

nodes.summary: If every reward `G k` is integrable, so is every `S n`.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope is integrable

nodes.summary: (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2: the expectation of (1.1.9) at `n = 0`). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space and any stopping time `τ ≤ N`, `E[G τ] ≤ E[S 0]`.
nodes.title: Every bounded stopping time earns at most the expected envelope at time zero

nodes.summary: The first meeting time attains the expected envelope at time zero (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2: the expectation of (1.1.10) at `n = 0`). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space, `E[G τ*] = E[S 0]`.
nodes.title: The first meeting time attains the expected envelope at time zero

nodes.summary: The first meeting time from `n` on is a stopping time.
nodes.title: The first meeting time from `n` on is a stopping time

nodes.summary: For a strongly adapted reward, `τ*` is a stopping time with respect to `𝒢`.
nodes.title: The first meeting time is a stopping time

nodes.summary: The Snell envelope dominates the reward up to the horizon (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.13)): `G n ≤ S n` everywhere for `n ≤ N`.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope dominates the reward up to the horizon

nodes.summary: The Snell envelope stopped at the first meeting time is a martingale (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.14) with `n = 0`). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space, `(S (k ∧ τ*))_k` is a martingale with respect to `𝒢`.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope stopped at the first meeting time is a martingale

nodes.summary: The first meeting time from `n` on attains the envelope conditionally (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, (1.1.10)). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space and `n ≤ N`, `S n = E[G τₙ | 𝒢 n]` almost everywhere, where `τₙ` is the first time in `[n, N]` at which `S = G`.
nodes.title: The first meeting time from `n` on attains the envelope conditionally

nodes.summary: (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.13)). Let `Y` be integrable with `E[Y (n + 1) | 𝒢 n] ≤ Y n` almost everywhere for `n < N` and `G n ≤ Y n` almost everywhere for `n ≤ N`. Then `S n ≤ Y n` almost everywhere for every `n ≤ N`. Adaptedness of `Y` is not needed.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope is the smallest supermartingale dominating the reward

nodes.summary: If `k < τ* ω` then `S k ω = E[S (k + 1) | 𝒢 k] ω`.
nodes.title: Before the first meeting time the envelope is the continuation value

nodes.summary: If `k < τ* ω` then `S k ω ≠ G k ω`.
nodes.title: Before the first meeting time the envelope exceeds the reward

nodes.summary: If `N ≤ n` then `S n = G N` (Peskir–Shiryaev, equation (1.1.6)).
nodes.title: The Snell envelope equals the final reward from the horizon on

nodes.summary: Before the horizon, `S n = max (G n) (E[S (n + 1) | 𝒢 n])` (Peskir–Shiryaev, equation (1.1.7)).
nodes.title: Wald–Bellman recursion for the Snell envelope

nodes.summary: `S τ* = G τ*` pointwise (Peskir–Shiryaev, equation (1.1.8)).
nodes.title: At the first meeting time the envelope equals the reward

nodes.summary: For a reward sequence `G`, a filtration `𝒢`, a measure `μ` and a horizon `N`, the Snell envelope is `S N = G N` and, for `n < N`, `S n = max (G n) (E[S (n + 1) | 𝒢 n])` (Peskir and Shiryaev, *Optimal Stopping and Free-Boundary Problems*, Birkhäuser 2006, Chapter I, equations (1.1.6)–(1.1.7)). After the horizon the sequence is frozen at `G N`, which keeps it a supermartingale on all of `ℕ`; the book only defines it…
nodes.title: Snell envelope by backward induction

nodes.summary: For `n ≤ N`, `τₙ = min {k ∈ [n, N] : S k = G k}` (Peskir–Shiryaev, equation (1.1.8)); for `n = 0` it is `snellStoppingTime`.
nodes.title: First time from `n` on that the Snell envelope meets the reward

nodes.summary: The first meeting time is the smallest optimal stopping time (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.12) with `n = 0`). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space, if a stopping time `τ ≤ N` is optimal, `E[G τ*] ≤ E[G τ]`, then `τ* ≤ τ` almost everywhere.
nodes.title: The first meeting time is the smallest optimal stopping time

nodes.summary: The first meeting time is at most the horizon.
nodes.title: The first meeting time is at most the horizon

nodes.summary: Optimality of the first meeting time (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.11) with `n = 0`). For a strongly adapted, integrable reward on a finite measure space and every stopping time `τ ≤ N`, `E[G τ] ≤ E[G τ*]`; hence `τ*` is optimal and the value `sup_{τ ≤ N} E[G τ]` equals `E[S 0]`.
nodes.title: Optimality of the first meeting time

nodes.summary: The stopping time `τ* = min {k ∈ [0, N] : S k = G k}` (Peskir–Shiryaev, equation (1.1.8) with `n = 0`); the set is nonempty because `S N = G N`.
nodes.title: First time the Snell envelope meets the reward

nodes.summary: If the reward is strongly adapted, each `S n` is strongly measurable with respect to `𝒢 n`.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope is adapted

nodes.summary: The Snell envelope is a supermartingale (Peskir–Shiryaev, Theorem 1.2, part (1.1.13)): for a strongly adapted reward with integrable values on a finite measure space, the Snell envelope is a supermartingale with respect to `𝒢`.
nodes.title: The Snell envelope is a supermartingale
